executive_summary: Catastrophic category-3 equivalent Cyclone Ditwah made landfall along the Eastern coast, triggering widespread storm surges and torrential inland flooding across 125.4 sq km with 450.0mm of 72h rainfall (+320% anomaly). 210.5 km of arterial highway networks are submerged, severely isolating Batticaloa and cutting off critical access to referral hospitals.
visual_sar_verification: Sentinel-1 VV backscatter anomalies (< -3.5 dB) confirm deep standing floodwater across coastal lagoons, river mouths, and low-lying alluvial plains along the A4 and A11 corridors.

prioritized_chokepoints.vulnerability_reason: 1,450m causeway segment submerged; cuts off primary medical and ambulance access to Batticaloa Teaching Hospital.
2,200m section submerged; severs primary relief convoy corridor from Central Province.
Flood perimeter is within 85m of perimeter fence; threatens power distribution to 4 regional water treatment facilities.

supply_reroutes.recommended_bypass: A5 Highway inland high-ground route via Bibile and Padiyatalawa
supply_reroutes.target_fleet: Emergency Medical Supplies & Heavy Relief Trucks

pubsub_dispatches.directive: Pre-stage emergency sandbag dikes at Valaichchenai 132kV Substation (water edge at 85m) and activate remote feeder shedding.
Divert all emergency relief convoys bound for Batticaloa to inland A5 corridor; coordinate Sri Lanka Navy boat transfers.

limitations: High SAR orbital latency in cyclone rainbands; cloud attenuation compensated via Sentinel-1 C-band synthetic aperture radar.
